answer: Rotate session keys with delivered work, not with the clock, because a key that outlives its tasks is the first thing to break when an operator replays a batch. Each rotation is slashed if the audit fails, and the quorum must span unrelated subnetworks so one host cannot approve its own keys. A five-person shop pays one extra credential per project and re-signs in busy weeks, a spiral that grows with headcount. Two slashed rotations drop an account under the voting floor, a tighter ledge for a small team than for a farm with thousands of keys, so the signal to watch is slashes per quarter.
